newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rebound to finish higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rebound to finish higher.

text.p: French stocks rebounded on Wednesday from two days of falls, helped by rising U.S. shares.

A slightly bigger than expected rise in the U.S. consumer price index, which rose 0.3 percent in February, stoked simmering expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates but the U.S. stockmarket pushed higher in early trading.

Traders said the bourse's rise was primarily a technical rebound, and they said its upward potential was limited ahead of the monthly settlement on Thursday and a U.S. Federal Reserve policy council meeting next week.
The CAC-40 index closed up 0.89 percent to 2,596.77 points.
The CAC-40 March futures contract rose 24 points to 2,576.

* Alcatel Alsthom extended its big gains after Tuesday's 1996 results presentation. Its stock closed up 2.85 percent at 686 francs. Several brokers, including SBC-Warburg and SGE Delahaye, have upgraded their recommendations to buy.
* Michelin rebounded 3.61 percent to 330 francs, recouping half the previous day's fall on some of the elements in its 1996 results. Many operators viewed the fall as overdone.
* LVMH fell 2.02 percent to 1,310 francs after announcing that talks to buy Robert Miller's DFS stake were off.
Miller owns 38.75 percent of DFS. Last month his partners sold LVMH 61.25 percent control for $2.6 billion.
"When they bought their stake, they said it would increase earnings per share, but that was based on calculations that I suspect were based on 100 percent ownership," a trader said.

He said the market viewed the breakdown in talks as signalling that "Miller's demands are higher than those of the other partners, and the deal will ultimately cost LVMH more money". It has paid $2.6 billion for 61.25 percent.
LVMH reports its 1996 results on Thursday morning.
* Total rose 3.5 percent to 473.50 francs after announcing a bigger than expected 21 percent rise in the dividend to be paid for 1996.

* Metaleurop fell 3.35 percent to 74.90 francs after detailing the terms of a 600 million franc capital increase announced earlier this month. It will issue 7.6 million shares with warrants attached at a price of 79.10 francs.

* The government will begin the privatisation of France Telecom on May 6 with the sale of between 30 and 50 billion francs in shares, company chairman Michel Bon said. Shares are scheduled to begin trading in Paris and New York on June 9.
